title: Blocked training facilitates learning of multiple schemas
construct: Learning several schemas (event structures) from experience, and how the order of training shapes it
paradigm: Coffee Shop World (schema learning from stories)
compared: accuracy of predicting the next event of a story after blocked vs interleaved training on two schemas; in a follow-up, blocked training early vs late
manipulated: when the blocked part comes (early vs late)
note: Each story is a short sequence of events; the context (which coffee shop) decides which event follows which, and the events themselves are shared between the two contexts. In the version used with the EGO model there are two contexts and two start states, and a story is context, start, then three events (context A: 1-3-5-7 and 2-4-6-8; context B: 1-4-5-8 and 2-3-6-7), so no single event tells the next one without the context. The design is the order of stories: the curriculum is the manipulation, so what a sequence must fix is the run length of each context, which start state and path occur how often in each context, and that the test stories mix the contexts. Details of the human experiments (number of stories, block length, response format) are in the paper; check them there before building.

title: Toward the Emergence of Intelligent Control: Episodic Generalization and Optimization
construct: Whether episodic memory with a learned context can explain fast learning and control (the EGO model)
paradigm: Coffee Shop World (schema learning from stories)
compared: a model's next-event prediction after blocked vs interleaved training, against the human advantage for blocked training
note: A modelling paper: it uses the Coffee Shop World as one of three domains. See the entry under implicit and statistical learning for the task.
